items.title: Most top Fed officials blame AI for fueling inflation. Not Trump's Fed chief.
items.excerpt: When President Donald Trump chose him to lead the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh argued that the artificial intelligence boom would help tame inflation. More than a dozen of his colleagues, including two other Trump appointees, now say it’s doing the opposite, playing a role in fueling inflation, which could soon mean even higher interest rates on credit cards, car loans and mortgages. Warsh will get a chance to revisit that argument on Monday, when he opens a conference in San Francisco meant to inform the work of a task force he created to study AI’s effects on jobs and productivity.

items.title: Fed’s Williams says central bank has ’work to do’ to get inflation back on target By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said on Thursday that more interest rate increases are likely as the US central bank seeks to lower high levels of inflation in an otherwise healthy economy. Williams did not say when he expects the Fed to raise rates again or how far it will go with the increases. “The economy is strong, labor market continues to strengthen, and inflation is persistent,” Williams said at the UC Berkeley Alumni Salon held in New York. “We’ll need to take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis,” he said, adding, “We still have work to do … to get monetary policy to the right place.” Financial markets broadly expect the central bank to increase its current 3.75% to 4% federal funds target rate range by a quarter percentage point at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in early December, and then to raise rates again in January. There’s an active debate about more aggressive action on the part of the Fed after this week’s stronger-than-expected inflation data. Core inflation rose 0.3% in October, a pace that Fed Governor Christopher Waller had earlier said would put a 50-basis-point hike on the table for December. But other Fed officials such as Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack have made a case for a more modest and steady pace of increases to allow the economy to adjust to the increase in short-term borrowing costs. FED CAN’T LOWER ABSOLUTE LEVEL OF ... Williams was asked about the elevated cost of living that has resulted from the surge in inflation over the last half-decade. He said there’s little the central bank can do about it. The central bank uses interest rates to affect the rate of change in prices rather than the absolute level of those prices. That means recent years’ inflation has left many in the economy struggling with a much higher overall level of prices. When it comes to lowering the price level, history shows that trying to “put the genie back in the bottle, that creates huge distortions and damage to the economy,” Williams said. ... “There are consequences of that” and it is a “higher cost of living,” the official said.

items.title: Goolsbee Urges Fed Vigilance After October CPI Rises 0.4% | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: By Miriam Hart Nov 13, 2026, 11:07 AM UTC ... Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee urged policymakers to watch for signs of an overheating U.S. economy after consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, with missing survey data limiting the annual comparison. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said its Consumer Price Index (CPI) for urban consumers rose 0.4% from September, after a 0.6% increase the month before. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, gained 0.3% for a third consecutive month. Shelter prices increased 0.3% and accounted for more than 30% of October’s overall monthly rise. BLS did not publish a 12-month change for the all-items CPI. The agency lacked October 2025 survey data after a lapse in appropriations and could not calculate the year-over-year comparison. The missing figure limits what the October release can show about the recent annual pace of headline inflation. Goolsbee described inflation as above the Federal Reserve’s goal, but the CPI figures do not by themselves establish that comparison. The Fed’s longer-run 2% goal is measured by the annual change in the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, a separate measure from CPI. In an interview published by Yahoo Finance on Nov. 12, Goolsbee said the latest increase “wasn’t a one-off month.” His concern, he said, was that unanchored expectations could contribute to a wage-price spiral that would be difficult and painful to reverse. Market-based measures had not yet shown expectations becoming unanchored, he said. Goolsbee also identified services and health care as persistent price pressures, which he said tariffs and oil prices did not explain. The comments followed his earlier public warnings about services inflation. His remarks called for vigilance about a possible risk; neither the interview nor the CPI release established that the economy was already overheating. The Federal Open Market Committee’s next meeting is scheduled for Dec.

items.title: Democrats, Trump administration prepare for rash of oversight probes
items.excerpt: Democrats are preparing for a knockout fight with the White House and the Department of Justice (DOJ) after a series of letters to legislative leaders saying the administration would seek to rebuff their probes. “I think Congress has to flex all of its power,” Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), the House Oversight Committee’s ranking member and incoming chair, said during an interview with CNN’s Kaitlan Collins, adding that Democrats would not be afraid to turn to the courts. “When you ask people across the country why they were motivated to vote and to bring change, they said the same two things: It was about affordability, and it was about rooting out government corruption. Well, we have a mandate to take on corruption, and certainly the corruption of the Trump family,” he continued. A White House letter to Garcia suggesting incoming probes risked becoming criminal in nature was not the only correspondence this week. Aaron Reitz, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, accused Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) on Wednesday of “terrorizing” entities when the senator contacted those who donated to President Trump’s ballroom construction project and other renovations. When Reitz directed Blumenthal, the incoming chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, to preserve his records for a potential future criminal probe, the senator shot back and demanded the same from the attorney. Both sides have accused the other of overreaching in a quickly escalating brawl before a single subpoena has been issued. “They are overstating their powers in a huge way and setting themselves up for embarrassment,” said Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), who is set to lead the House Judiciary Committee and has fired off more than 200 letters requesting information during the last two years he led the panel in the minority. The law is largely on the side of the incoming Democrats, as Congress’s investigatory powers have been upheld by the Supreme Court; laws bar obstruction of their efforts; and members themselves are afforded broad protections from the speech or debate clause. The letters, however, signal the pressure from the White House to push back on the coming investigations. Reitz’s letter came after Bloomberg News reported a tense call the DOJ led with the nation’s 93 U.S. attorneys, including a reference for the need to take a “wartime” stance going forward and telling the appointees they should be prepared to resign if they are not ready to carry out ... Now back in control of the House, Democrats have renewed access to the courts, able to file litigation on behalf of the House in a way they were during the majority.

items.title: Shygirl, Moby Drop New Songs for 'Club Kid' Soundtrack
items.excerpt: November 13, 2026 ... Shygirl, Moby, and Brutalismus 3000 contributed new songs to EP Club Kid (Music From & Inspired by the Film), the soundtrack to Jordan Firstman’s recent film Club Kid. Released by A24 Music, the five-track EP also includes two distinct covers of Arthur Russell’s “The Boy with a Smile” by Christine and the Queens and Nirosta Steel. Shygirl, who appears as herself in the film, offered ethereal song “Waves,” which comes on the heels of her second studio album Swallow!. Moby offered “I Want a Rocket,” a dance floor-ready number with a pulsating beat. Club Kid, now in select theaters, stars Firstman, Reggie Absolom, and Diego Calva. It debuted at Cannes earlier this year.

items.excerpt: - Nov 13, 2026 - Nov 13, 2026 Updated 2 hrs ago Spielberg says he has the same enthusiasm as he did making 8 mm movies as a boy NEW YORK (AP) — Steven Spielberg's passion for filmmaking remains as strong as ever. The admired director was honored at the Museum of Modern Art’s film benefit Thursday. Spielberg reflected on his career and shared that his enthusiasm for storytelling hasn't faded since he was 12. Spielberg has made over 35 feature films, from “E.T.” to “Schindler’s List.” He says stories often find him, sparking his creativity. The MoMA event celebrated his contributions, with appearances by Martin Scorsese and Tom Cruise. Spielberg emphasized filmmaking as a collaborative effort, acknowledging those who have shared his journey. Rosalía wins album of the year 2026 at the Latin Grammy Awards for 'Lux,' capping a thrilling night Rosalía has won album and song of the year at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards. She also opened the Thursday night show. Juanes won the first award for best pop/rock album. Performers at this year’s bash included Karol G, Anitta, Jorge Drexler and Silvana Estrada. The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards’ person of the year was Daddy Yankee. He became the first Latin urbano artist to receive the honor. He ripped through his biggest hits an hour into the evening, treating the award show stage like a stadium floor. Edgar Barrera became the most awarded person in the show’s history with 30 career wins. Lang Lang had to age like red wine before releasing a complete set of Beethoven piano concertos Star Chinese pianist Lang Lang has recorded all five Beethoven piano concertos after more than 25 years on the classical music circuit. Deutsche Grammophon announced on Friday the release for March 5, featuring recordings with conductor Andris Nelsons and the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra. The release coincides with the 200th anniversary of Beethoven's death. Lang Lang, known for his crossover appeal, has collaborated with artists like Sting and Metallica. He says he feels more mature now, influenced by past recordings and experiences. ... Movie Review: Johnny Depp’s dour 'Ebenezer' is a horror-tinged holiday slog Johnny Depp takes on Ebenezer Scrooge in the new film "Ebenezer," hoping to add a unique twist to the classic tale. Director Ti West uses modern horror elements to revamp Charles Dickens' story. Associated Press critic Mark Kennedy says Depp's portrayal includes oddball character traits, reminiscent of his past roles, but with a darker twist. The film features eerie scenes, like street lamps going out and graveyard zombies, but also unexpected moments, like a cast performance of "Silent Night." Despite its creative attempts, the movie struggles to find its footing or say anything new. "Ebenezer" is rated PG-13 and releases on Friday. Godzilla returns in special-effects glory in the latest movie with an anti-war message TOKYO (AP) — Japan’s most famous monster is back in “Godzilla Minus Zero” in all its fire-breathing, stomping glory, delivering its trademark allegorical message of the destruction of nuclear war and the pathos of human folly. Takashi Yamazaki, the director, writer and head of special effects, told The Associated Press in an interview that Godzilla is “a metaphor for war and nuclear weapons,” reflecting the uncertainties in people's hearts. Yamazaki also directed “Godzilla Minus One,” released three years ago, which won the Oscar for best visual effects. The new movie is proving to be a huge hit, topping $31.6 million over the opening weekend, a record debut for a foreign-language film at the North American box office. Gram Parsons celebrated in song by Emmylou Harris, Elvis Costello on eve of his Rock Hall induction WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Gram Parsons, the country-rock pioneer, is being honored with a musical tribute as he enters the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 53 years after his death. Artists like Elvis Costello, Sheryl Crow and Emmylou Harris performed his songs Wednesday night at the Troubadour club in Los Angeles. Harris, who had a brief but impactful partnership with Parsons, sang “Love Hurts” and other classics. Parsons, who died in 1973, is credited with influencing the country-rock genre. His daughter, Polly Parsons, emphasized his lasting impact on alternative country and Americana music. Maika Monroe shows how much more than 'Scream Queen' she is in 'Victorian Psycho' CANNES, France (AP) — After years spent fleeing serial killers and worse, Maika Monroe is on the offensive. In the gothic thriller “Victorian Psycho,” she plays a deranged governess. On the surface, the movie appears to extend Monroe’s reputation as the preeminent “Scream Queen” of her generation thanks to movies like “It Follows” and “Longlegs.” Bodies get bloody in “Victorian Psycho,” too, but Monroe’s deranged protagonist is hysterically funny as she finally turns the tables in this gleefully morbid gothic thriller. Maiko told The Associated Press that this is the character she enjoyed the most. “Victorian Psycho” opens in theaters Friday.
